Correto. In woven (immature) bone, osteocyte lacunae are irregularly arranged within the matrix which lacks lamellae. Lacunae are rounder than are those in mature bone and the matrix has a more bluish tint due to the proteoglycans in the matrix and reduced collagen fiber content. Woven bone is not as strong as lamellar bone.

alternativas.feedback: Correto. Mature bone is organized in lamellae with orderly arranged lacunae located between the lamellae. Lamellar bone can be arranged as cylindrical structures, seen here, called Haversian systems (osteons) or as flattened plates on the surface of bone (inner and outer circumferential lamellae). Mature bone is highly eosinophilic due to the large number of collagen fibers in the matrix.
alternativas.feedbackOriginal: Mature bone is organized in lamellae with orderly arranged lacunae located between the lamellae. Lamellar bone can be arranged as cylindrical structures, seen here, called Haversian systems (osteons) or as flattened plates on the surface of bone (inner and outer circumferential lamellae). Mature bone is highly eosinophilic due to the large number of collagen fibers in the matrix.
